key_insight: Faynt shows that a single Transformer policy can be scaled and optimized to control all 26 Super Smash Bros. Melee characters and achieve strong competitive performance.
engineering_relevance: The paper demonstrates a practical recipe for multi-character game AI that combines large-scale replay pretraining, distillation, curriculum learning, and low-latency inference.
method: Pretrained 10M and 75M Transformer policies on about 840,000 human replays.
Applied post-training with rank- and outcome-based curricula, 75M-to-10M distillation, and Fox mirror-match RL.
Optimized inference on recorded game states to support real-time decision making.
evidence_signal: On the 152-game benchmark, the supervised 10M won 69.7% of games, and after RL it won 240 of 244 same-character games (98.4%) against 14 baselines, plus all 68 games against a zero-delay Slippi-AI model.
watch_item: The authors note they did not isolate the effect of Faynt’s zero added delay versus opponents’ 21- or 24-frame delays, so fairness and latency effects remain a confound.
paper_title: Faynt: Scaling and Optimizing Policies for Competitive Melee
